title: Warframe
provenance: verified locally on Apple Silicon (M-series), engine sikarugir-10.0_6, Highball 0.7.21
notes: Apply the warframe recipe first: it turns DirectWrite off for the game's launcher only (Tools\Launcher.exe), whose embedded browser otherwise paints a black window on this engine, the same DirectWrite problem as Sikarugir #255. With that override the launcher shows its EULA, updates the game and starts it. The game itself needs nothing. Use DXMT: the first tutorial mission, with combat, ran at about 35 fps at 1728x1117 borderless (the game's own low preset, 1280x720 render, anti-aliasing and ambient occlusion off) with the Metal HUD reading 28 ms of GPU per frame; later in the same session, past the tutorial, the maintainer's own play ran above 100 fps by the HUD. DXVK also reaches the mission but is GPU-bound at about 16 fps (51 ms GPU) with the same settings. 'Login with Steam' works; a Steam account without a Warframe account gets the game's own bind-or-create dialog, which is normal. A sleeping display stalls the game for as long as it sleeps, so keep the Mac awake for long sessions. Verified 2026-09-04 on macOS 26.6.2, M1 Pro: launcher update, Steam login, account creation, tutorial mission. Clean exit was not checked.

anticheat.note: anti-cheat present; Linux/Proton support does not extend to macOS — userspace path works for some titles

dxmt.detail: tutorial mission at about 35 fps, 28 ms GPU per frame, 1728x1117 borderless with the low preset; above 100 fps later in the session (2026-09-04, r1, macOS 26.6.2, M1 Pro)

dxvk.detail: reaches the same mission but GPU-bound at about 16 fps, 51 ms GPU per frame, same settings
